papers.title: Wake-activated neuronal populations that regulate sleep drive.
papers.summary: Identified wake-activated neurons in the anterior medial preoptic area and median raphe that regulate sleep drive in mice. Activation of these cells induces recovery-like sleep, while their inhibition reduces sleep and abolishes increased sleep propensity; co-inhibition of GABAergic and serotonergic neurons chronically reduces sleep by ~70% without compensatory sleep drive.

papers.title: Nyx: a flexible framework for sleep scoring across species, lifespan and modalities.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Nyx is an unsupervised, PCA-based framework that clusters epochs into sleep states without training. Validated on ~8,000 hours across 19 datasets, it generalizes across species, lifespan, and modalities, matching human inter-scorer agreement, and enables NREM subtype classification and real-time closed-loop manipulation.

papers.title: Propofol-Facilitated Recovery Sleep Modulates Cognitive Function via Slow Oscillation-Spindle Coupling After Acute Sleep Deprivation in Rats.
papers.summary: In a rat model, propofol-facilitated recovery sleep after acute sleep deprivation improved spatial and recognition memory, increased slow oscillation density, and strengthened phase-accurate SO-spindle coupling, accompanied by reduced cortical NKCC1/KCC2 ratio.

papers.title: Enriched experience increases reciprocal synaptic connectivity and coding sparsity in higher-order cortex.
papers.summary: In mice, 10 weeks of enriched environment increased bidirectional excitatory synaptic connections in higher-order cortex and sparser, more orthogonal population activity during rest and sleep, supporting attractor network predictions.

papers.title: ThermoClock:A Novel Automated Temperature Regulation Device that Can Model Circadian Entrainment and Disruption in 2D and 3D in Vitro Models.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: ThermoClock, a low-cost Arduino-based device, delivered temperature cycles that entrained circadian reporters in U2OS cells and skin explants, with ramp time critical for entrainment strength. Short T-cycles disrupted rhythms, reduced cell migration in wounded explants, and wounding resetting depended on prior entrainment state.

papers.title: Nardilysin fine-tunes the mammalian circadian clock through selective modulation of PER2 function
papers.summary: The study identifies nardilysin (NRDC) as a modulator of the circadian clock. NRDC deficiency increased PER2 levels, shortened behavioral rhythms, and NRDC associated with PER2/CRY2, antagonizing PER2-mediated repression, with enrichment at E-box regions, linking nuclear proteolysis to circadian control.

papers.title: Diphenhydramine Disrupts Sleep Architecture in 5XFAD Alzheimer's Disease Model and Wild-Type Mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Chronic diphenhydramine treatment in 5XFAD and wild-type mice fragmented NREM2 sleep, increased NREM1 and REM during the active phase, and exacerbated sleep deficits in 5XFAD mice, questioning its use as a sleep aid in AD.

papers.title: Neural Signatures of Conscious Experience During Sleep: A Serial Awakening Study Using High-Density EEG
papers.summary: Using high-density EEG and serial awakenings in 140 participants, dreaming during NREM sleep was associated with reduced alpha/delta power and increased gamma measures, plus altered network organization. Machine learning classified dream vs. no experience with ROC-AUC 0.80.

papers.title: Circadian rhythms of neuronal and astrocytic glutamate transporters in the suprachiasmatic nucleus of mice.
papers.summary: This study examined circadian rhythms of neuronal (VGLUT1, VGLUT2) and astrocytic (GLAST) glutamate transporters in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) of mice under different lighting conditions. VGLUT1 and GLAST peaked during the light phase, VGLUT2 during the dark phase, and these rhythms persisted in constant darkness and light, indicating circadian control.

papers.title: The Human Intracerebral EEG Platform: A Cloud-Based Trusted Research Environment for Collaborative SEEG Research in Epilepsy and Neuroscience.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and implementation of the Human Intracerebral EEG Platform (HIP), a cloud-based trusted research environment for collaborative SEEG data sharing and analysis, now hosting 34 institutions and 10 projects.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment reduces displacements and reorganises circadian patterns: a putative indicator of positive welfare in dairy calves.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of environmental enrichment (brushes) on the diurnal activity patterns and aggressive behavior of pre-weaned dairy calves. Enriched calves showed higher diurnality and fewer feeder displacements, suggesting that these measures could serve as automated indicators of positive welfare.

papers.title: Wearable Electrodermal Activity Reveals Sustained Sympathetic Responses to Sleep Arousals
papers.summary: This study analyzed synchronized polysomnography and wrist-worn electrodermal activity from 100 adults to characterize sympathetic responses during sleep arousals. They found that arousals elicit sustained EDA modulation persisting up to 40 s post-arousal, primarily driven by clustered sympathetic bursts and amplitude enhancement, providing a quantitative baseline for tracking sympathetic dynamics.

papers.title: Pathophysiology of developmental and/or epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep: A diagnostic framework.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the pathophysiology of developmental/epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep (D/EE-SWAS). It proposes a diagnostic framework integrating sleep EEG, MRI, genomic sequencing, and neuropsychological assessment, highlighting the importance of slow-wave activity and spindle preservation.

papers.title: Circadian clock regulates intestinal epithelial cell differentiation via NOTCH/Hes1 oscillations.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigated circadian regulation of intestinal epithelial cell differentiation. RNA-seq revealed NOTCH signaling under circadian control, and Hes1 oscillations varied with stemness. Paneth cell numbers fluctuated over the circadian cycle, suggesting circadian-regulated Hes1 drives IEC composition dynamics.

papers.title: When the biological clock is disordered: circadian rhythm disruption as a core pathophysiological mechanism in anxiety and depression.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that circadian rhythm disruption is a core pathophysiological mechanism in anxiety and depression, integrating five key pathways (SCN-limbic circuit, HPA axis, immune inflammation, neurotransmitter plasticity, gut-brain axis). It also defines actionable subtypes of disruption, summarizes chronotherapies, and discusses controversies and future directions for precision psychiatry.

papers.title: In Two Minds about Lifelong Learning: Exploring Hemispheric Redundancy and Specialisation in Neural Models
papers.summary: The paper proposes a 4-module macroarchitecture inspired by memory consolidation, sleep, and hemispheric asymmetry, achieving competitive accuracy on Split-MNIST (98.3%), Split-Fashion-MNIST (84.9%), and Split-CIFAR-100 (29.29%).

papers.title: EFS-NET: EEG-fNIRS multi-scale fusion network based on spatial calibration.
papers.summary: The authors propose EFS-Net, an end-to-end multi-scale fusion network combining EEG and fNIRS with spatial calibration, which outperforms unimodal and traditional fusion models on two public datasets, achieving up to 81.69% accuracy.

papers.title: Chronic Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Hippocampal Cellular Remodeling through microglial polarization imbalance and neural functional disconnection.
papers.summary: Using single-cell RNA sequencing in mice, chronic intermittent hypoxia caused time-dependent hippocampal remodeling, with biphasic microglial response, neuronal loss, oligodendrocyte expansion, and rewired intercellular communication, implicating microglial polarization imbalance via HIF-1/p53 pathways as a central node.

papers.title: Abnormal local markers of sleep homeostasis in patients with focal epilepsy.
papers.summary: In patients with focal epilepsy, high-density EEG showed higher slow-wave activity and steeper slow-wave slopes compared to controls, with local theta extremes discriminating patients (AUC=0.84), and left-lateralized epileptiform discharges were associated with reduced overnight slow-wave decline.

papers.title: Multidimensional Microstate Alterations and Interpretable Classification of Electrical Status Epilepticus During Sleep Using Multi-Channel EEG.
papers.summary: The study developed a microstate-based EEG framework identifying ESES-related alterations in microstates B and C, with reduced flexibility and increased regularity, and a five-feature logistic regression model achieved promising classification accuracy.

papers.title: Plasma ALKBH5 depletion during severe intermittent hypoxia and its attenuation by galectin-3 inhibition: an experimental rat study.
papers.summary: In rats, severe intermittent hypoxia reduced plasma ALKBH5 levels, while galectin-3 inhibition with modified citrus pectin attenuated this reduction and reduced hypoxia-induced myocardial injury.

papers.title: Physiological Signatures Derived from Wrist Accelerometry Improve Detection of Isolated REM Sleep Behavior Disorder.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study developed a machine learning model using 876 accelerometry-derived physiological features from wrist sensors to detect isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD). The model achieved a subject-level AUC of 0.955 under leave-one-cohort-out validation, outperforming a movement-only model, and combined with a questionnaire reached 72% sensitivity with no false positives.

papers.title: Machine learning to detect intraoperative ischemia from electroencephalography in carotid endarterectomy surgery.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study evaluated machine learning models for automated detection of cerebral ischemia during carotid endarterectomy using quantitative EEG features. Random forest achieved the highest sensitivity (0.79-0.83) and XGBoost the highest specificity (0.93-0.96), with alpha-band activity and hemispheric asymmetry as key predictors.

papers.title: Cross-Regulation Between DNA Methylation and Circadian Clock Reprogramming in Ovarian Cancer: Mechanistic Insights, Biomarker Potential, and Therapeutic Implications.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the bidirectional interplay between DNA methylation and circadian clock reprogramming in ovarian cancer, discussing mechanistic insights, biomarker potential, and therapeutic implications. It highlights challenges and future directions including time-resolved sampling and single-cell epigenomics.

papers.title: Sleep architecture and lying behavior in horses across age groups and two housing systems: an overnight non-invasive EEG study.
papers.summary: The study used a non-invasive EEG mask to compare sleep architecture and lying behavior in horses across age groups and two housing systems over four nights, finding significant differences in sleep stages and lying behavior between systems and age groups, with younger horses showing more REM sleep and longer lying episodes. These findings suggest that housing conditions and age should be considered when assessing equine sleep and well-being.

papers.title: Faecalibacterium prausnitzii-derived L-arginine ameliorates insomnia by inhibiting POMC-ACTH-cortisol axis.
papers.summary: Integrating metagenomics and mouse models, the study found that Faecalibacterium prausnitzii-derived L-arginine alleviates insomnia by suppressing the POMC-ACTH-cortisol axis, restoring sleep and normalizing corticosterone levels.

papers.title: Transdiagnostic effects of combined sleep-circadian interventions on depressive symptoms and sleep outcomes in adults with mental disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 RCTs assessed the effects of combined sleep-circadian interventions on depressive symptoms and sleep outcomes in adults with mental disorders, finding significant improvements in depressive severity, insomnia, sleep quality, and functional impairment, though evidence certainty ranged from very low to moderate. The results provide promising transdiagnostic evidence for these interventions.

papers.title: [Mechanism of acupuncture regulating cAMP signaling pathway to improve ovarian dysfunction in sleep-deprived mice].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.summary: This study investigated the mechanism of acupuncture in alleviating sleep deprivation-induced ovarian dysfunction in mice. Transcriptomics and experimental validation showed that acupuncture regulates the cAMP signaling pathway, increasing ovarian cAMP content and expression of key molecules (FSHR, CREB1, ADCY5, PRKACA), thereby improving ovarian function.

papers.title: EEG-ECeG Coherence Mapping of Human Cerebro-cerebellar Projections: An Exploratory Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory study used wavelet coherence between EEG and electro-cerebellogram (ECeG) recordings during finger movements in six healthy adults to non-invasively map crossed cerebro-cerebellar projections. They found significant movement-related delta/theta-band coherence distributed contralaterally and frontally for cerebellar seeds, supporting the value of ECeG for studying cerebro-cerebellar connectivity.

papers.title: Contemporary Sedation Strategies for Mechanical Ventilation: Balancing Patient Outcomes, Delirium Prevention, and Early Recovery.
papers.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
papers.summary: This review discusses contemporary sedation strategies for mechanically ventilated patients, highlighting a shift from deep sedation to lighter protocols with daily interruptions and spontaneous breathing trials to reduce delirium and ICU-acquired weakness. It covers pharmacological options, monitoring techniques, and implementation frameworks like the ABCDEF bundle, emphasizing non-pharmacologic interventions and tailored approaches for special populations.

papers.title: Engineering a Timing-Accurate VR-EEG-Oculomotor Fusion System for Objective Assessment of Executive Function in ADHD.
papers.summary: This study engineered a timing-accurate VR-EEG-oculomotor fusion system for objective ADHD assessment, synchronizing a VR version of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test with EEG and eye/head tracking in 101 children. The best early-fusion deep neural network achieved 83% accuracy, demonstrating the system's potential as a scalable screening tool.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of a novel digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia application versus zolpidem: An exploratory randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: An exploratory randomized controlled trial compared a 5-week digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (dCBT-I) app with zolpidem in chronic sleep-onset insomnia. Both improved sleep onset latency at week 5, but dCBT-I showed sustained improvement at week 10 while zolpidem showed slight recurrence, with no significant between-group differences at week 5.

papers.title: Comparative evaluation of gut health, inflammatory factors, and sleep quality among shift workers: A cross-sectional study.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 200 shift workers found that night-shift workers had significantly more gastrointestinal symptoms, higher gut permeability markers (LPS, zonulin), elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, TNF-α), and poorer sleep quality compared to day-shift workers. The findings suggest night-shift work is associated with disrupted gut health, systemic inflammation, and sleep disturbances, indicating a need for lifestyle interventions.

papers.title: Separating early and intermediate vision EEG signatures of facial emotion recognition in a fast divided attention task to eye and mouth features.
papers.summary: In a fast divided attention task with 20 participants, EEG recordings showed that the P100 ERP was not sensitive to facial emotion, while N170 amplitude and latency were modulated by emotion (larger for happy) and P250 amplitude was lower for sad faces. These findings support distinct roles for early and intermediate visual processing in facial emotion recognition.

papers.title: Pharmacological treatments of REM sleep behaviour disorder in synucleinopathies: a systematic review of effectiveness and safety.
papers.summary: A systematic review assessed pharmacological treatments for REM sleep behavior disorder in synucleinopathies. Evidence for clonazepam and melatonin is limited and inconsistent, with clonazepam raising safety concerns; larger randomized trials are needed.

papers.title: Validation of intraoperative processed electroencephalography and cerebral oximetry for prediction of postoperative delirium in cardiac surgery: a prospective observational study.
papers.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
papers.summary: This prospective observational study of 148 cardiac surgery patients validated combined intraoperative monitoring with NIRS and processed EEG (pEEG) to predict postoperative delirium. Four states defined by these monitors showed associations: longer time in states with cerebral desaturation and/or deep anesthesia increased delirium odds, while a state with desaturation and deep anesthesia increased time to persistent organ dysfunction.

papers.title: The stress-fascia-pain axis in myofascial pain syndrome: a mechanistic integrative review and conceptual synthesis.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on myofascial pain syndrome, proposing a stress-fascia-pain axis that integrates trigger-point biochemistry, fascial biomechanics, stress-related neuroendocrine changes, and central sensitization. The authors suggest this framework explains heterogeneity and supports multimodal treatment, though evidence strength varies across domains.

papers.title: Analysis of psychomotor latency, spatial reasoning, and metabolic health markers in adolescent gamers: A comparative study of the impact of the confounding triad of sleep, diet, and screen modality.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
papers.summary: This comparative cross-sectional study of 200 male adolescents found that gamers had faster psychomotor reaction times and better spatial reasoning than non-gamers, with dose-dependent improvements from gaming hours, but poor sleep negatively impacted performance. Dietary caloric intake was a stronger predictor of adiposity than gaming, suggesting that metabolic risks are more related to diet than to gaming itself.

papers.title: New-Onset Convulsive Status Epilepticus Temporally Associated With Accidental Inhalation of Billygoat Weed (Ageratum conyzoides) Smoke: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A case report describes a 76-year-old man who developed new-onset convulsive status epilepticus shortly after inhaling smoke from burning Ageratum conyzoides (billygoat weed). Extensive workup revealed no other cause, and the patient recovered fully, suggesting a potential neurotoxic trigger.

papers.title: Neuroprotective Effects of Rauwolfia vomitoria Against 3-nitropropionic Acid-induced Motor Impairment and Oxidative Stress in Mice.
papers.summary: This study in mice examined the neuroprotective effects of Rauwolfia vomitoria against motor impairment and oxidative stress induced by 3-nitropropionic acid, a mitochondrial toxin. Treatment with the plant extract improved motor coordination and reduced oxidative stress markers, suggesting potential for movement disorder therapy.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
